chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The sign of the liar is that he informs you with news of the sky and the earth, and the east and the west; so when you ask him about the prohibitions of Allah and His permissible things, there is not anything with him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the sign of a liar according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between mere knowledge of the unseen (al-ghayb) and true religious authority, critiquing those who boast of cosmic insights but fail in practical jurisprudence (fiqh). It underscores the principle that authentic divine connection is validated by adherence to Halal and Haram, a key criterion for evaluating claimants of knowledge in the absence of the Infallibles. This serves as a practical test for believers to discern genuine scholars from charlatans who prioritize spectacular claims over substantive legal understanding.
